extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying creative writing evaluation, computational creativity, and LLM-generated fiction (NLP/CHI/creative-writing scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric (TTCW) for evaluating creativity in short fictional stories: 14 binary (Yes/No) tests organized into four Torrance-inspired dimensions (Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, Elaboration). Each test requires a short written rationale and the final creativity score is the aggregate number of tests passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLUENCY (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures the volume of meaningful ideas and smooth execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers five tests assessing pacing, scene vs exposition balance, use of literary devices, ending quality, and overall understandability/coherence. Applied to evaluate how many meaningful ideas are present and how smoothly the story executes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: FLEXIBILITY (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures diversity of perspectives and adaptive approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers three tests assessing perspective/voice variety, emotional balance between interiority/exteriority, and structural turns that are surprising yet appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORIGINALITY (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers three tests focused on originality in theme/content, originality of thought (absence of clichés), and originality in form/structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ELABORATION (dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures depth and granularity of detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers three tests evaluating sensory-level worldbuilding, character development complexity, and rhetorical/multi-level meaning (surface and subtext).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the manipulation of time in terms of compression or stretching feel appropriate and balanced?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLUENCY: assess whether temporal manipulation (compression/expansion) feels appropriate and balanced to support meaning and engagement. Raters must provide a 1–3 sentence rationale explaining why they judged Yes or No.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene vs Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story display awareness and insight into the balance between scene and summary/exposition?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLUENCY: evaluate whether the story shows an appropriate balance between dramatized scenes and summary/expository passages. Provide a short written rationale (1–3 sentences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Proficiency & Literary Devices
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story make sophisticated use of idiom or metaphor or literary allusion?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLUENCY: judge the sophistication and effectiveness of idiom, metaphor, allusion, and overall language proficiency. Include a brief rationale describing examples or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the end of the story feel natural and earned, as opposed to arbitrary or abrupt?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLUENCY: determine whether the ending follows organically from the story's development and feels earned. Rationale should explain how the ending succeeds or fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandability & Coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do the different elements of the story work together to form a unified, engaging, and satisfying whole?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLUENCY: assess overall coherence and whether elements integrate into a satisfying narrative. Raters must justify their binary choice with a short explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective & Voice Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story provide diverse perspectives, and if there are unlikeable characters, are their perspectives presented convincingly?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLEXIBILITY: evaluate diversity of viewpoint and the convincingness of perspectives, including for morally ambiguous or unlikeable characters. Provide a 1–3 sentence rationale citing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story achieve a good balance between interiority and exteriority, in a way that feels emotionally flexible?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLEXIBILITY: judge the balance between characters' inner life (interiority) and outward actions/description (exteriority) and whether emotional tone adapts appropriately. Short justification required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story contain turns that are both surprising and appropriate?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of FLEXIBILITY: assess whether plot/structure contains well-calibrated surprises or turns that feel fitting rather than arbitrary. Rationale should indicate examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Theme and Content
rubrics_metrics.description: "Will an average reader of this story obtain a unique and original idea from reading it?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of ORIGINALITY: determine whether the story conveys a distinct, novel idea to a general reader. Raters must explain briefly what is original or why it is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is the story an original piece of writing without any clichés?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of ORIGINALITY: evaluate avoidance of clichés and presence of fresh thinking. Provide short rationale highlighting clichés or original turns of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Form & Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story show originality in its form?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of ORIGINALITY: judge whether the story's formal or structural choices display originality. Raters should cite structural elements that support their judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: World Building and Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the writer make the fictional world believable at the sensory level?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of ELABORATION: assess sensory detail and believability of setting/world. Short written rationale required describing sensory evidence or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does each character in the story feel developed at the appropriate complexity level, ensuring that no character feels like they are present simply to satisfy a plot requirement?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of ELABORATION: evaluate character complexity and whether characters serve as fully-realized agents rather than mere plot devices. Provide a concise rationale with examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does the story operate at multiple 'levels' of meaning (surface and subtext)?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary (Yes/No) judgment. Part of ELABORATION: judge whether the story offers layered meanings and subtext beyond surface narrative. Short justification required indicating layers or absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration Format and Scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Each test receives a binary judgment (Yes/No) accompanied by open-ended written rationale (1-3 sentences minimum). Final creativity assessment reflects the aggregate number of tests passed, not individual test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required procedure: for every story, annotate all 14 tests with Yes/No and provide a 1–3 sentence rationale per test. The overall creativity score is the count of passed tests (aggregate). This scoring model emphasizes breadth across dimensions rather than weighting individual tests.
